inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalent (1 ADS = 7 Class A ordinary shares), fully diluted. 6,755.2m ordinary shares at 2026-02-28 (20-F FY2025 line 3974) less ~152.6m repurchased to 2026-06-30 (21.8m ADS) = ~6,603m ordinary = ~943m ADS, plus ~17m ADS for in-the-money nominal-strike options/RSUs (613.8m options outstanding at a US$0.25/share weighted strike are mostly out of the money). 960m is also the Q2-2026 weighted average (6,714.7m / 7 = 959.2m). Held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows. The three convertible tranches are far out of the money and are carried as debt, not shares.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow add-back, identical to the 'Share-based compensation expenses' line of the non-GAAP reconciliation (IQ_6K_Q4-2025.txt). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buybacks were nil. 163.6 is the treasury-stock balance at 2026-06-30 (US$24.1m, 21.8m ADS) under the US$100m programme adopted March 2026. The flat count is therefore only partly funded, and by a company whose debt exceeds its cash.
inputs.fx_note: USD/CNY 6.6712 (Yahoo CNY=X, 2026-11-15) -> model-to-quote 0.1499 USD per CNY. Per-ADS values are computed in CNY and converted at that rate. No dual listing exists yet for a parity check (the Hong Kong secondary listing is filed confidentially, not live). Balance-sheet items are at the 2026-06-30 statement values; the company's own convenience rate at that date was 6.7851.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.0% in CNY for all three scenarios. China 10-year government yield ~2% plus a ~7% equity risk premium (mature-market premium plus China country premium) at a beta of ~1.2 gives a cost of equity near 10.5%; debt costs 4.6-6.5% on the USD convertibles and bank loans. A market-weight blend would be nearer 8%, but the equity cushion is thin and the debt is short-dated, so the rate is held close to the cost of equity. Leverage, the short-drama threat and VIE/ADR risk are charged in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, not through a further premium or per-scenario rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B by construction. US GAAP operating-lease cost is already inside operating expenses and therefore inside the margin path; operating lease liabilities (410.5 at 2026-06-30) are excluded from net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is zero to avoid a second charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Ignored. Non-controlling interests are a 90.4 deficit balance at 2026-06-30 and NCI profit share has been within +/-45 a year; no deduction and no credit.
inputs.net_debt_composition: 2026-06-30 carrying values: short-term loans 1,945.7 + long-term loans current 1,600.4 + long-term loans 3,546.7 + convertible notes current 1.1 + convertible notes 6,615.2 = 13,709.1; less cash 3,205.9, restricted cash 0.5, short-term investments 917.5 = 4,123.9. Amounts due to Baidu (2.4bn at FY2025, up from 2.0bn in FY2023) are accrued bandwidth and cloud charges, treated as operating payables, not debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with the non-US adaptations, on the Drivers route. iQIYI is a consumer-internet operating company, not a financial, and is neither in receivership nor under a going-concern qualification, so an enterprise-value build with the debt deducted in full is the right frame; the leverage shows up as a small equity residual and a bear case where the equity is worth nothing, not as a different model. CONTENT IS AN OPERATING COST: cash paid for licensed and produced content sits in operating cash flow and its amortisation in cost of revenues, so 'ebitda_margin_path' here is non-GAAP operating margin plus depreciation of fixed assets and amortisation of non-content intangibles only (FY2023 ~12.8%, FY2024 8.9%, FY2025 3.1%, trailing twelve months to Q2-2026 ~0.6%). Content cash spend is assumed equal to amortisation over the horizon (FY2025 spend 11.6bn against 13.1bn amortised, FY2024 13.7bn against 13.4bn). OWNER FCF: last_fcf follows the house formula on reported FY2025 FCF, which is after 628.1 of cash interest paid; the unlevered equivalent is about -100 (10.0 + 628.1 - 334.4 - 403.4). Trailing-twelve-month reported FCF to Q2-2026 is 165.8, flattered by payables rising 770 in H1-2026. PAG LOAN: the US$636.6m receivable is a loan to the holder of the US$522.5m PAG convertible notes, who has pledged those notes back to iQIYI as security; the notes repay at 130% of principal (US$679m) on 2028-01-01, so the two positions largely offset. The notes are in total debt at carrying value and the loan is added in the equity bridge at principal; its interest is stripped from the flows. ANCHOR VINTAGE: Q3-2026 results are scheduled for 2026-11-16, one day after this valuation; net debt, the share count and the year-one driver should be refreshed against that release. The price is a regular-session close at a 52-week low.
warnings: Q3-2026 results are due 2026-11-16; the balance-sheet anchors here are 2026-06-30.
The bear scenario is on the terminal-value floor: owner cash flow never turns positive and the equity is worth nothing on that path.
A Hong Kong secondary listing raising US$200-300m at the current price would add roughly 25-40% to the share count; it is not in the share path.

equity_bridge.item: Loan receivable from PAG at principal (US$636.6m at 6.7851)
equity_bridge.note: IQ_6K_Q2-2026.txt line 132; secured by a pledge of the PAG Notes, which are inside total_debt. Interest on it is excluded from the flows.
Book 1,775.5 at 2026-06-30. Unlisted equity-method and fair-value stakes impaired or marked down by 340, 176 and 72 in FY2023-FY2025; their income is not in the flows. The 50% haircut is a judgment.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not usable: book equity rose from 6.3bn (FY2022) to 13.3bn (FY2025) through the January 2023 follow-on offering and convertible activity while the accumulated deficit widened to 44.6bn. Revenue has shrunk about 2% a year and is down 14% from the FY2023 peak.
historical_growth.notes: EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined because the end points are negative or straddle zero. Unlevered owner FCF (reported FCF plus cash interest paid, less interest income and SBC) was about 3,205 in FY2023, 1,893 in FY2024 and -100 in FY2025: 10.1%, 6.5% and -0.4% of revenue. GAAP operating margin went 4.5% (FY2022), 9.4%, 6.2%, 0.8% (FY2025) and -1.5% over the twelve months to Q2-2026.

base.rationale: Year one is FY2026: H1 revenue fell 9.4% and Q2 5%; two second-half quarters near 6.25bn give about 25.0bn. Mature owner EBIT margin of 4.0% (6.0% less 1.2% SBC and 0.8% D&A) sits between the FY2025 result (0.8%) and the FY2023-FY2024 level (9.4%, 6.2%), and close to the FY2022-FY2025 average of 5.2%.

bull.rationale: Margin returns to between the FY2024 (8.9%) and FY2023 (12.8%) levels on this definition; revenue regains the FY2023 peak only in year ten.

bear.rationale: Content cost stays near 15bn a year against falling revenue, as it did in FY2024-FY2026; owner EBIT stays at or below zero and shrinking deferred revenue drains cash.

scenario_narratives.base: Long-form streaming in China is a shrinking pool of attention, and iQIYI stops losing its share of it. Membership and advertising revenue settle after the FY2026 decline, the 'other' line stays at its reset level, and revenue holds near 24-26bn. The margin recovers part of the way, because content cost, which stayed near 15bn while revenue fell by more than 4bn, is finally cut through fewer and cheaper titles and AI-assisted production. Owner EBIT reaches 4% of revenue, below FY2023-FY2024 because short-drama competition caps pricing. The convertibles and bank loans are refinanced, with the PAG loan repaid against the PAG Notes in January 2028. On these flows the enterprise is worth little more than the debt.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI production toolkit and the creator-led platform do what management says: content cost per hour falls materially, short-form drama becomes a second paying franchise rather than a substitute, and one or two hit seasons restore membership growth. Revenue grows 3-4% a year from FY2028 and the margin returns to the FY2023-FY2024 range. Debt is refinanced on better terms and the Hong Kong listing broadens the holder base without a deeply dilutive raise. This needs the content slate, the cost programme and the capital markets to cooperate at once.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hongguo, Douyin, Kuaishou and Tencent's short-drama push keep taking viewing time; iQIYI's subscribers and advertisers follow. Revenue falls every year, content cost cannot be cut as fast without accelerating churn, and owner cash flow stays negative. With 13.7bn of debt, most of it due or puttable by March 2028, the company refinances only through a heavily dilutive equity raise or support from Baidu on Baidu's terms. The model's terminal value is on the zero floor: the operations are worth less than the debt and ADS holders are left with nothing or close to it.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30%, double the house default: three of the last four quarters were operating losses, debt is 13.7bn against 4.1bn of liquid assets with a 2028 maturity wall, and the recovery rests on an unproven AI and short-drama pivot. Base 45%: partial margin recovery is the central case because content cost is a management decision and was cut successfully in 2022-2023. Bull 25%, below the 35% default: it needs a better slate, lower content cost and open capital markets together, though the 2023 margin shows the level is attainable.

valuation_philosophy.summary: iQIYI is valued as an operating company whose enterprise value is close to its debt. The three scenarios differ mainly in one driver, the operating margin after content cost, and small changes in it move the equity from nothing to more than twice the current price. The valuation is therefore a statement about leverage: the ADS behaves like an option on a margin recovery, and the probability-weighted value should be read with the bear case in view rather than as a point estimate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Operating margin after content cost: each percentage point of mature margin is worth roughly 1.5-2bn of enterprise value against about 5.3bn of market capitalisation.
Refinancing: US$522.5m PAG Notes (repayable at 130%) mature 2028-01-01, the 2028 Notes mature and the US$350m 2030 Notes are puttable in March 2028.
Equity issuance: a Hong Kong raise of US$200-300m at the current price would dilute holders by roughly a quarter to two fifths and is not modelled.
PAG loan recoverability: the bridge credits 4.3bn at principal on the strength of the pledged notes; the security has not been tested.
Payables as funding: accounts payable and amounts due to Baidu rose about 1.1bn in FY2025 and H1-2026, supporting reported cash flow.
VIE structure, Baidu control and US-listed China ADR risk, none of which is charged separately.
CNY/USD: the flows and most assets are in CNY, the convertibles and the quote are in USD.
valuation_philosophy.limited_liability_caveat: The engine reports a negative per-ADS value where net debt exceeds enterprise value. A shareholder cannot lose more than the price paid, so a negative scenario value should be read as zero when judging the payoff; the weighted value on that reading is given in the hand-off report.
